source.title: Reinforcement Learning with Backtracking Feedback
source.authors: Bilgehan Sel; Vaishakh Keshava; Phillip Wallis; Lukas Rutishauser; Ming Jin; Ding-Cheng Li

page_placements.theme: Training recovery beyond the opening can improve robustness

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. There are minor PDF text-extraction artifacts; the reported tables are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures harmful-output attack success under Middle Filling, GCG, and decoding-parameter attacks, using attack-success rates rather than the original claim’s proposed token-position KL measure.
record.gate_note: The paper discusses shallow safety and cites prior work, but those cited findings are not rows. It reports no aligned-versus-base per-token KL, compliant-opening prefill test, few-shot harmful or benign fine-tuning test, or weight-localization result. Rows below are the paper’s own attack-success-rate results for tested attack settings.
record.test_reason: This is mainly a defense paper (RLBF, BSAFE+). Its own baseline measurements still bear on V4: the instruction-tuned and plain-RL models it evaluates are bypassed by Middle Filling, GCG suffixes and decoding-parameter attacks (Tables 1–2). These use attack-success rates rather than the originals' exact prefill setup, hence T2. Results for the authors' own methods (BSAFE+, RLBF) and the Circuit Breakers defense baseline are method comparisons, not tests of a version.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors also frame the high IT/RL ASR under Middle Filling as evidence of 'shallow safety'. They claim RLBF holds against an adaptive GCG, preserves utility (MMLU/BBH/GSM8K/MATH), and that its gains persist with a weaker critic.
record.recipe_differences: The paper develops RLBF and BSAFE+ rather than reproducing the cited few-example fine-tuning or token-position KL methods; it trains a backtracking behavior using SFT and critic-feedback RL.
record.method_sensitivity: Attack type and benchmark change the reported outcome. Model family and size vary in Table 1. The paper also reports that a weaker critic yields 2%–4% LMSYS ASR versus 1%–2% with the stronger critic, while LMSYS-MF results are comparable (Section 5.5).

fits_no_version.finding: Training models to emit a backtrack signal anywhere mid-generation (RLBF) cuts ASR to 1–7% under MF, GCG and decoding attacks. ASR is unchanged under an adaptive GCG that suppresses backtrack tokens. Disabling mid-generation backtracking raises LMSYS ASR from 1% to 7%, and disabling all backtracking raises it to 18%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In-generation backtracking or recovery training at arbitrary positions resists attacks that get past the response opening (a V7-adjacent defense result from the authors' own method).

record.problems: The reported attack-success tables provide no uncertainty estimates. Table 2 does not specify model-level disaggregation in the presented values. The paper does not directly measure refusal rates or token-position KL, and it does not test compliant-opening prefills.
record.rows_left_out: Table 2 results for RL, Circuit Breakers, and BSAFE+ on GCG were omitted to stay within 60 rows; the corresponding reported results are in Table 2 (RL: 62.6% and 38.3%; Circuit Breakers: 10.7% and 13.4%; BSAFE+: 6.6% and 5.7% for AdvBench and HEx-PHI, respectively). The remaining Table 2 rows were retained for IT, RLBF, and BSAFE+ decoding comparisons.

untested.parts: No benign fine-tuning with a harmful-compliance measure.
No per-token KL or position analysis.
No compliant-opening prefill attack. MF injects harmful content after a benign start, and its exact construction is not fully specified.
No analysis of why alignment is shallow.
No measure of safety depth across token positions. RLBF is the authors' own backtracking defense, so its results are not treated as a test of deepening.

missing.what: RL and Circuit Breakers decoding-parameter ASR (RL 81.8%/51.7%, CB 2.0%/12.4% on MaliciousInstruct/HEx-PHI). Not declared in rows_left_out. The RL values are additional V4 evidence.
Adaptive GCG that also suppresses backtracking tokens: RLBF unchanged at 4.7%/4.3%, BSAFE+ shifts by at most 0.4 points.
Backtracking ablation: RLBF 1%, without backtracking 18%, without mid-generation backtracking 7% on LMSYS.

record.verdict_notes: Only the IT/RL baseline attack results bear on V4. The reader's limits_scope label on the defense rows is dropped: the defenses' lower ASR does not qualify V4, which concerns standard aligned models. The no-attack LMSYS rows are baselines, not V4 results. ASR is judged by a critic covering subtle violations (bias, toxicity, misinformation), so it is broader than harmful-request compliance. Table 2 does not say which models were evaluated. No uncertainty is reported.

versions.untested_parts: No fine-tuning on a few to a few hundred harmful examples or resulting refusal/compliance measurement.
No fine-tuning on ordinary or carefully selected benign data with harmful-compliance measurement.
No per-token KL measurement between aligned and base models.
Tests Middle Filling, GCG suffix attacks, and decoding-parameter attacks, but not a compliant-opening prefill. Reports harmful-output attack success, not refusal rates directly.
No weight or rank localization, ablation of a small parameter set, or parameter-level safety measurement.
Does not test whether data or training objectives produce first-token shallowness.
Trains a backtracking mechanism and evaluates robustness, but does not measure whether safety becomes distributed beyond the first response tokens or test that depth directly.

relationships.condition: Gemma 2 (2B, 9B) and LLaMA 3 (1B, 3B, 8B) instruction-tuned and plain-RL models under Middle Filling, GCG suffix and decoding-parameter attacks
relationships.reason: IT/RL ASR rises from 22–28% with no attack to 61–81% under MF (T1-MF-IT-*, T1-MF-RL-*). IT reaches 65.6%/36.5% under GCG and 84.3%/54.9% under decoding attacks (T2-GCG-IT-*, T2-DEC-IT-*).
relationships.display_finding: Under Middle Filling, ASR rose from 22–28% with no attack to 61–81%. Instruction-tuned models reached 65.6% and 36.5% under GCG and 84.3% and 54.9% under decoding attacks.

source_check.reason: The supporting label is warranted, but its condition overattributes Table 2 results to named model sizes. T1-MF-IT-* and T1-MF-RL-* support V4 across the five listed sizes under MF. T2-GCG-IT-ADV, T2-GCG-IT-HEX, T2-DEC-IT-MI and T2-DEC-IT-HEX support V4 for unspecified model configurations. Table 2 supplies neither model identities nor an aggregation procedure. The LMSYS and LMSYS-MF rates also do not establish a paired no-attack-to-attack increase.

relation.reason: Tables 1–2 measure baseline models' susceptibility to attacks that bypass safety, independently of the proposed defense's performance.

tranche.reason: Baseline attack evaluations test V4 using Middle Filling, GCG and decoding manipulations; the study does not reproduce the original token-position KL or fine-tuning experiments.

source_check.notes: Table 1's ordinary LMSYS harmful subset is not a documented matched no-attack control for LMSYS-MF; retain explicit IT-versus-RL comparator baselines rather than substituting those cross-set rates. ASR includes nuanced safety violations; Table 2's model identities and aggregation are unspecified.

statements.correction: RLBF ASR: MF 3–7%; GCG 4.7% AdvBench, 4.3% HEx-PHI; decoding attacks 1.0% MaliciousInstruct, 3.7% HEx-PHI. Adaptive GCG optimizing suppression of backtracking tokens: unchanged 4.7% AdvBench and 4.3% HEx-PHI. Table 5 directly disables backtracking tokens in an LMSYS ablation: ASR 18% without backtracking, 7% without middle-generation backtracking, versus 1% full RLBF.
statements.problem: The low ASRs are correct, but the claimed failure under adaptive GCG contradicts Section 5.1.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: IT and RL models under Middle Filling, GCG, and decoding-parameter attacks
reader_labels.reason: Attack success is substantial for these tested baselines: Table 1 reports 61%–81% for IT/RL on LMSYS-MF and 22%–28% for IT/RL on LMSYS; Table 2 reports 36.5%–84.3% for IT models on the listed GCG and decoding tests (rows T1-MF-IT-*, T1-MF-RL-*, T1-LM-IT-*, T1-LM-RL-*, T2-GCG-IT-*, T2-DEC-IT-*).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Circuit Breakers, BSAFE+, and RLBF on the tested attack settings
reader_labels.reason: Attack success remains nonzero but is much lower for these methods; BSAFE+ and RLBF report 3%–7% on LMSYS-MF, RLBF reports 1%–2% on LMSYS, and RLBF reports 1.0%–4.7% on the Table 2 tests (rows T1-MF-CB-*, T1-MF-BS-*, T1-MF-RB-*, T1-LM-CB-*, T1-LM-BS-*, T1-LM-RB-*, T2-GCG-RB-*, T2-DEC-RB-*, T2-DEC-BS-*).
